chain_trace.break_detail: The log's verdict pattern ('same-order alignment broken', 'entries appear swapped') is contradicted by the log's own raw evidence: batch result[0] id set == single-face by-id 1 id set and batch result[3] id set == single-face by-id 6 id set, so no swap occurred and order alignment held; the true content of the primary observation is by-id self-absence, which is (a) outside the contract's same-order clause and (b) explicit by-design behavior in source (collection_query.rs excludes referenced point ids via must_not HasId). The contract->doc->script links are intact; the break is between the log's Type4 order-violation label and the raw observation's actual semantics.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST src/actix/api/query_api.rs query_points_batch (line 110 route POST /collections/{collection_name}/points/query/batch) -> for request_item in searches { batch.push((request, shard_selection)) } (lines 136-155, order-preserving) -> dispatcher.toc().query_batch -> lib/collection/src/collection/query.rs query_batch (line 445): resolve_referenced_vectors_batch resolves by-id queries' ids to vectors -> try_into_shard_request per request applies exclude_referenced_ids (must_not HasId of referenced ids, INCLUDING the by-id query's own id) -> do_query_batch_impl returns results via transposed_iter(all_shards_results).zip(requests_batch.iter()) (line 315-317) and try_join_all preserves group order (line 519-523) -> query_api.rs maps responses 1:1 in order (lines 167-185). Mechanism found: a {"query": <id>} request resolves the id's vector AND excludes that id from candidates — so by-id results never contain the queried point, on both single and batch faces. Order of batch results is structurally preserved end-to-end (no swap mechanism exists).
